findings.fact: ATLOP learns input-dependent TH and uses strict comparison for multilabel predictions; its adaptive-threshold objective differs from BCE.
LOP multiplies subject/object pretrained attention, sums heads and normalizes token weights; no learned relation-specific quantum query.
Thresholding rule without its intended loss is not an interchangeable inference improvement; this is a paper-reported DocRED result, not Q-RMEA evidence.
Posthoc perclass threshold dev gains do not carry to the reported test in this setup; no general theorem about all threshold tuning.

primary_interpretation: At fixed shared scores with null ties, singlelabel max-positive-vs-TH rule equals original40argmax.
For one positive y, a=exp(z0-zy), b=sum_negative exp(zr-z0), CE=log(1+a+ab), ATL=log((1+a)(1+b)); they are generally different.
Renaming learned null score supplies no new decision rule; known loss adaptation remains a possible baseline, not selected same-core L5.
